answer: Temporal State Snapshot Routing Each identity must solve a unique computation bound to a specific block-header hash, crossing a computational canyon before submission. The system writes this proof to an immutable append-only ledge, invalidating the solution instantly for future blocks. Because the target changes every cycle, an attacker cannot reuse the same output and must spend fresh processing power for every single sybil address. This forces a recurrent energy expense rather than a one-time registration fee. An added optical pigment verification step ensures hardware uniqueness per node.
